summary: Austria is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806) can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and nationals on the EU's visa-required list (Annex I) need a Schengen short-stay visa (€90 under the Visa Code, or €35 for Armenian, Azerbaijani and Belarusian nationals and €67.50 for Cabo Verdean nationals under EU visa facilitation agreements). Longer stays run through the national Visa D or a residence title such as the Red-White-Red Card.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Austria: the Schengen Borders Code counts stays on the territory of all the Member States together.
Driving on Austrian motorways requires a vignette (€12.80 for 10 days, €106.80 for a year; digital or sticker). ASFINAG charges a €200 substitute toll for a car or camper van without one.
Once ETIAS starts, the EU says applications are made on the official ETIAS website or the official ETIAS mobile app; it is not yet in operation.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Austria?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Austria and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does an Austria Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11 under the Visa Code; under EU visa facilitation agreements Armenian, Azerbaijani and Belarusian nationals pay €35 and Cabo Verdean nationals €67.50. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries. Austria's national Visa D costs €195 (€97 for children under 6) under the Fees Act.

faq.question: What is Austria's Red-White-Red Card?
faq.answer: It is an Austrian residence and work title for non-EU workers. On the skilled-workers-in-shortage-occupations route, migration.gv.at says eligibility is assessed on points, the card is generally issued for 24 months, it entitles you to work for the employer named in the application, and the application fee is €218.

faq.question: Do I need a vignette to drive in Austria?
faq.answer: Yes. All motorways and expressways require a vignette: €12.80 for 10 days, €32 for 2 months or €106.80 for a year (2026 car prices), as a sticker or digital vignette. Driving without one means paying a €200 substitute toll.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Austria without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area.
